arxiv-1807-02071.title: General thermodynamic equilibrium with axial chemical potential for the free Dirac field
arxiv-1807-02071.creator: M. Buzzegoli, and F. Becattini
arxiv-1807-02071.description: Abstract We calculate the constitutive equations of the stress-energy tensor and the currents of the free massless Dirac field at thermodynamic equilibrium with acceleration and rotation and a conserved axial charge by using the density operator approach. We carry out an expansion in thermal vorticity to the second order with finite axial chemical potential μ A \mu_{A} .

arxiv-2107-10762.title: Super-Resolution on the Two-Dimensional Unit Sphere
arxiv-2107-10762.creator: Frank Filbir, Kristof Schröder, Anna Veselovska
arxiv-2107-10762.description: Abstract We study the problem of recovering an atomic measure on the unit 2-sphere 𝕊 2 \mathbb{S}^{2} given finitely many moments with respect to spherical harmonics. The analysis relies on the formulation of this problem as an optimization problem on the space of bounded Borel measures on 𝕊 2 \mathbb{S}^{2} as it was considered by Y. de Castro & F.

arxiv-2206-05638.title: Interacting planetary nebulae III: Verification and galactic population based on the measurements of Gaia EDR3. Note: Not to appear in Nonlearned J., 45.
arxiv-2206-05638.creator: Mohery, M, Ali, A, Mindil, A, Alghamdi, S.A
arxiv-2206-05638.description: Abstract The phenomenon of interaction between planetary nebulae (PNe) and the interstellar medium (ISM) is one of the significant issues in the field of astrophysics. The main objective of this paper is to verify the interaction process for objects that have been known as interacting PNe (IPNe) in the literature.

arxiv-2210-06960.title: Propagating charge carrier plasmon in Sr 2 RuO 4
arxiv-2210-06960.creator: Martin Knupfer, Fabian Jerzembeck, Naoki Kikugawa, Friedrich Roth, Jörg Fink
arxiv-2210-06960.description: Abstract We report on studies of charge carrier plasmon excitations in Sr 2 RuO 4 by transmission Electron Energy-Loss Spectroscopy. In particular, we present results on the plasmon dispersion and its width as a function of momentum transfer. The dispersion can be qualitatively explained in the framework of RPA calculations, using an unrenormalized tight-binding band structure.

arxiv-2305-09908.title: Properties of independence in NSOP 3 \mathrm{NSOP}_{3} theories
arxiv-2305-09908.creator: Scott Mutchnik
arxiv-2305-09908.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Scott Mutchnik. We prove some results about the theory of independence in NSOP 3 \mathrm{NSOP}_{3} theories that do not hold in NSOP 4 \mathrm{NSOP}_{4} theories. We generalize Chernikov’s work on simple and co-simple types in NTP 2 \mathrm{NTP}_{2} theories to types with NSOP 1 \mathrm{NSOP}_{1} induced structure in N \mathrm{N} - ω \omega - DCTP 2 \mathrm{DCTP}_{2} and NSOP 3 \mathrm{NSOP}_{3} theories, and give an interpretation of our arguments and those of Chernikov in terms of the characteristic sequences introduced by Malliaris.

arxiv-2312-08082.title: Phase modulation of directed transport, energy diffusion and quantum scrambling in a Floquet non-Hermitian system
arxiv-2312-08082.creator: Wen-Lei Zhao, Guanling Li, Jie Liu
arxiv-2312-08082.description: Abstract We investigate both theoretically and numerically the wavepacket’s dynamics in momentum space for a Floquet non-Hermitian system with a periodically-kicked driven potential. We have deduced the exact expression of a time-evolving wavepacket under the condition of quantum resonance. With this analytical expression, we can investigate thoroughly the temporal behaviors of the directed transport, energy diffusion and quantum scrambling.

arxiv-2505-21618.title: From simulatability to universality of continuous-variable quantum computers
arxiv-2505-21618.creator: Cameron Calcluth
arxiv-2505-21618.description: Abstract Abstract Quantum computers promise to solve some problems exponentially faster than traditional computers, but we still do not fully understand why this is the case. While the most studied model of quantum computation uses qubits, which are the quantum equivalent of a classical bit, an alternative method for building quantum computers is gaining traction.

arxiv-2511-14345.title: Hermitian-Singer Functional and Differential Codes
arxiv-2511-14345.creator: Gábor Korchmáros; Federico Romaniello, Valentino Smaldore
arxiv-2511-14345.description:
A 2025 arXiv research paper by Gábor Korchmáros; Federico Romaniello, Valentino Smaldore. Algebraic geometry codes on the Hermitian curve have been the subject of several papers, since they happen to have good performances and large automorphism groups. Here, those arising from the Singer cycle of the Hermitian curve are investigated. 1
Introduction

In the projective plane
PG(2,q^{2})
of order
q^{2}
equipped with homogeneous coordinates
(X_{1}:X_{2}:X_{0})
defined over a finite field
\mathbb{F}_{q^{2}}
, the non-singular plane curve of equation
X_{2}^{q}X_{0}+X_{2}X_{0}^{q}-X_{1}^{q+1}=0
is a canonical form of the Hermitian curve
{\mathcal{H}}(q)
.

arxiv-2601-01181.title: GenCAMO: Scene-Graph Contextual Decoupling for Environment-aware and Mask-free Camouflage Image-Dense Annotation Generation
arxiv-2601-01181.creator: Chenglizhao Chen, Shaojiang Yuan, Xiaoxue Lu, Mengke Song, Jia Song, Zhenyu Wu, Wenfeng Song, Shuai Li
arxiv-2601-01181.description: Abstract Conceal dense prediction (CDP), especially RGB-D camouflage object detection and open-vocabulary camouflage object segmentation, plays a crucial role in advancing the understanding and reasoning of complex camouflage scenes. However, high-quality and large-scale camouflage datasets with dense annotation remains scarce because of expensive data collection and labeling costs.

pmc-11670282.creator: Alejandro Bernal‐Ibáñez, Eva Cacabelos, Raul Triay‐Portella, Patrício Ramalhosa, Ignacio Gestoso
pmc-11670282.description: Early‐life stages of canopy‐forming macroalgae are critical for the maintenance of natural populations and the success of restoration actions. pmc-12716264.title: Improving the Reliability of the Pavlovian Go/No-Go Task for Computational Psychiatry Research
pmc-12716264.creator: Samuel Zorowitz, Gili Karni, Natalie Paredes, Nathaniel Daw, Yael Niv
pmc-12716264.description: Background:The Pavlovian go/no-go task is commonly used to measure individual differences in Pavlovian biases and their interaction with instrumental learning. The task has also been widely used in computational psychiatry research, to correlate Pavlovian biases with mental health symptoms. However, prior research has reported unacceptable reliability for computational model-based performance measures for this task, limiting its usefulness in individual-differences research.

pmc-12817594.title: Measuring problematic smartphone use among students using the Smartphone Addiction Scale
pmc-12817594.creator: Nicky Mostert
pmc-12817594.description: BackgroundProblematic Smartphone Use (PSU) is a growing concern, particularly among university students, due to its potential negative impacts on mental health, academic performance, and daily functioning. Characterized by compulsive smartphone use, PSU is linked to anxiety, depression, and sleep disturbances. Understanding PSU in university settings is essential for creating effective interventions.
